item.title: From a digital Wild West to strict age limits: do social-media bans actually protect teens?
item.description: Many EU member states are working on social media bans individually, before any EU-wide measure — but is banning social media, only for kids, and one country at a time, the best move?

item.title: THIS WEEK: Clock is ticking for Russian sanctions deal in time for Ukraine war anniversary
item.description: Fourth-anniversary Russian sanctions, plans for Gaza under Donald Trump's Board of Peace, Friedrich Merz in China, and domestic EU curbs on firearms are all on the table this week.

item.title: Listen: Are we serious about regulating AI?
item.description: The EU needs to regulate smartly if it wants to have a real impact. Because globally, the US and China — the two biggest AI players — are not regulating AI use.

item.title: EU should strike now Trump tariffs have been defeated by Supreme Court
item.description: With Friday's Supreme Court verdict Donald Trump is off balance and on the defensive. The moment is opportune to stand up to his bullying tactics. He has not looked this vulnerable since he was reeling from the market reactions to his initial Liberation Day tariffs.

item.title: The EPP lets slip the real reason for the NGO witch-hunt
item.description: Why do some centre-right European People's Party MEPs, supported by the far-right, continue to centre the debate on funding for NGOs? The real end goal here is discrediting and defunding NGOs in order to sideline them even further in political decision-making.

item.title: Orbán’s sanctions veto revives talk of EU legal retaliation against Hungary
item.description: Hungarian foreign minister Szijjártó's Russia veto claims rubbished as "amazing ... shocking ... disgrace" in Brussels on Monday.

item.title: Data protection watchdogs worldwide call for safer AI content, after Grok scandal
item.description: The European Data Protection Board, along with 60 other data protection authorities around the globe, have called for safeguards on AI content-generators, especially regarding non-consensual AI imagery.

item.title: EU halts US trade pact pending ‘clarity’ on tariffs from Washington
item.description: MEPs have scrapped plans to vote on the EU-US trade deal on Tuesday, amid the 'chaos' of the new Donald Trump trade tariffs unilaterally announced at the weekend following a Supreme Court defeat.

item.title: Four years of war: Don’t buy Putin’s ‘bullshit’, Ukraine ambassador tells EU
item.description: Ahead of the fourth anniversary of Russia’s full-scale invasion, Ukrainian ambassador to the EU Vsevolod Chentsov warned that achieving peace with Russia requires real pressure on Moscow, cautions against normalising the war or engaging in 'premature' EU talks with Moscow, and sets the case for full EU membership.

item.title: Rights chief warns EU’s ‘safe country’ move puts asylum protections at risk
item.description: "The idea that you can send somebody or people to another country without individual assessment is a violation of basic refugee law," human rights commissioner Michael O’Flaherty told EUobserver.
